concerns.text: Tasks T044, T045, and T046 implement 'higher-order topological features' (motifs, spectral gap) and 'reviewer response' workflows. These features are not present in spec.md (FR-001 only lists degree distribution, clustering, average path length) or plan.md. There is no FR/SC or User Story in the spec authorizing this scope, leaving these tasks without a requirement anchor.

Tasks T047 and T048 extend the regression pipeline to include 'higher-order metrics' as predictors. Since the spec (FR-004) and plan do not define these metrics as required predictors, these tasks lack a corresponding Functional Requirement or User Story to satisfy.

Tasks T049 and T050 generate visualizations for 'higher-order metrics' and 'comparative visualizations'. The spec (US-3) only mandates heatmaps for 'topological features' (defined in FR-001 as standard metrics) and does not require comparative plots for unapproved higher-order features. These tasks have no matching spec element.

Task T051 updates 'research.md' to discuss 'higher-order metrics' and 'reviewer feedback'. The spec and plan do not include a requirement to update research documentation based on reviewer feedback regarding higher-order metrics, as these metrics were never part of the approved scope. This task lacks a spec anchor.

Task T016b implements timeout detection for 'any single network exceeds 6 hours'. SC-004 defines the timeout constraint for the 'full simulation and analysis pipeline for 10+ networks'. The task description does not explicitly link to SC-004 or clarify if it is an implementation detail of the full pipeline check, creating a potential traceability gap for the specific success criterion.

Task T017b describes implementing 'manual verification comparison logic' for SC-003. SC-003 requires 'manual verification' of the first 5 networks. The task focuses on the *logic* to perform the check rather than the *execution* of the manual verification or the generation of the evidence artifact required to prove SC-003 is met. The mapping is weak.
